summary: Optimizing LLM usage at inference time can reduce API spend by 50-80% in production systems while simultaneously improving latency, letting teams scale AI without proportional cost growth. The highest-leverage techniques are prompt caching (up to 90% input cost reduction), semantic caching, model routing, and prompt compression. Most savings come from avoiding redundant token processing and matching the right-sized model to each task.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (provider-native)
techniques.description: Reuse static portions of prompts (system instructions, few-shot examples, large context) across requests so the provider only charges full price for the dynamic part. The cached prefix is billed at a steep discount and processed faster.
techniques.savings: up to 90% reduction on cached input tokens
techniques.example: Place your long static system prompt and tool definitions at the start of every request and enable cache_control (Anthropic) or rely on automatic caching (OpenAI) so repeated prefixes cost a fraction of full input price.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Cache responses keyed by the semantic meaning of a query (via embeddings) rather than exact string match, returning stored answers for semantically similar questions and skipping the LLM call entirely.
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache to embed incoming queries; if a new query's embedding is within a similarity threshold of a prior one, serve the cached answer instead of calling the model.

techniques.name: Model Routing / Tiered Model Selection
techniques.description: Route simple requests to small, cheap models and reserve large expensive models only for hard tasks, using a classifier or heuristic to decide per-request.
techniques.example: Send FAQ-style or classification prompts to gpt-4o-mini or Claude Haiku and only escalate to GPT-4o or Claude Opus when the cheap model's confidence is low or the task is flagged complex.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Reduce the number of input tokens by trimming redundant words, summarizing context, removing filler, or using compression tools like LLMLingua that drop low-information tokens while preserving meaning.
techniques.example: Run long retrieved documents through LLMLingua to compress them 3-5x before injecting into the prompt, cutting input tokens with minimal quality loss.

techniques.name: Output Token Limiting & Control
techniques.description: Cap max_tokens, request concise formats (JSON/bullets), and explicitly instruct brevity so the model generates fewer—and typically more expensive—output tokens.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=200 and add 'Respond in under 3 sentences' to avoid the model producing long rambling answers that inflate output billing.

techniques.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Context Trimming
techniques.description: Instead of stuffing entire documents into context, retrieve and pass only the most relevant chunks, drastically reducing input tokens per query.
techniques.example: Use a vector store to fetch the top-3 relevant passages for a question and pass only those instead of the full 50-page manual.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Combine multiple independent tasks into a single call or use provider batch APIs that process requests asynchronously at a large discount.
techniques.savings: up to 50% reduction via batch API pricing
techniques.example: Submit overnight bulk classification jobs through OpenAI's Batch API to get ~50% off standard token pricing with a 24h completion window.

techniques.name: Streaming & Early Stopping
techniques.description: Stream responses and stop generation as soon as the needed information appears (via stop sequences), avoiding paying for unnecessary trailing tokens and improving perceived latency.
techniques.example: Define a stop sequence like '###END' so the model halts generation immediately after producing the required answer block.

techniques.name: Few-Shot to Zero-Shot Reduction
techniques.description: Trim or eliminate verbose few-shot examples once the model performs well zero-shot or with a fine-tuned/instruction-tuned prompt, removing large repeated input blocks.
techniques.example: Replace five in-context examples with a single crisp instruction after validating accuracy stays acceptable, cutting the fixed prompt overhead.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching layer for LLM queries that stores and retrieves responses by embedding similarity to cut redundant API calls.

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK to call 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, model routing, fallbacks, and cost tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; Enterprise plan with SSO/support (custom pricing)

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform offering caching, cost tracking, rate limiting, and request logging via a drop-in proxy.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); Pro from ~$20/mo, Enterprise custom

tools.name: Redis (Semantic Cache / LangCache)
tools.description: In-memory data store providing vector-based semantic caching for LLM responses with very low latency, usable via RedisVL or managed LangCache.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; Redis Cloud from ~$5/mo, Enterprise custom

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in caching (InMemory, Redis, SQLite, GPTCache integrations), prompt management, and RAG utilities.

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression library that reduces prompt length by removing low-information tokens while preserving task performance.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway with semantic caching, smart model routing, load balancing, fallbacks, and observability for production LLM apps.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; Pro from ~$49/mo, Enterprise custom

tools.name: Martian / OpenRouter
tools.description: Model routing and marketplace gateways that automatically direct requests to the cheapest capable model across many providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-as-you-go pass-through pricing with small markup/margin

quick_wins: Enable provider-native prompt caching and move all static system/instruction/context content to the front of your prompts to cut input costs up to 90%.
Switch high-volume, simple tasks from a flagship model to a cheaper small model (e.g., gpt-4o-mini or Claude Haiku) for 40-80% blended savings.
Set max_tokens limits and ask for concise outputs to stop paying for unnecessary expensive output tokens.
Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of your LLM to serve repeated/similar queries without an API call.
Move non-real-time bulk jobs to provider Batch APIs for roughly 50% off standard token pricing.
